2607.18496.title: Towards an Automated Test of LLM Security Knowledge
2607.18496.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for a range of software, hardware and human-centered security tasks. Consequently, LLM performance on security tasks is an active area of measurement and research, often with a focus on identifying areas in which LLM security ``knowledge'' may be insufficient. Popular strategies for identifying LLM security knowledge gaps include building corpora of challenge questions or task benchmarks, strategies that require substantial manual work and security expertise to design and execute. We introduce a partially-automated method for assessing LLM knowledge of a security area.The method uses authoritative information from Consumer Protection Agencies (CPAs) to identify instability in LLM responses that can be indicative of knowledge gaps. We demonstrate the method for 2 security topics, identity theft and impostor scams, and 5 LLMs in 2 leading LLM families, Gemini and GPT, using publicly available information about identity theft and impostor scams from 6 CPAs.The method distinguishes between models that have and don't have sufficient knowledge to accurately identify the security topics in text narratives.
2607.18496.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地用於各種軟體、硬體和以人為中心的安全任務。因此，LLM在安全任務上的表現成為一個活躍的測量和研究領域，通常專注於識別LLM安全“知識”可能不足的領域。識別LLM安全知識缺口的常見策略包括建立挑戰問題或任務基準的語料庫，這些策略需要大量的手動工作和安全專業知識來設計和執行。我們引入了一種部分自動化的方法來評估LLM在某一安全領域的知識。該方法利用消費者保護機構（CPAs）的權威信息來識別LLM回應中的不穩定性，這可能表明知識缺口。我們展示了該方法在兩個安全主題——身份盜竊和冒名頂替詐騙——以及在兩個主要LLM家族（Gemini和GPT）中的五個LLM上的應用，使用來自六個CPAs的有關身份盜竊和冒名頂替詐騙的公開信息。該方法區分了具有和不具有足夠知識以準確識別文本敘述中安全主題的模型。
